newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - May 7.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - May 7.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sri Lankan press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

Agricultural and industrial sectors have recovered after last year's drought and power cuts, investments appear to gather momentum as reflected in domestic private sector credit and foreign participation in stock market, Deputy Finance Minister G.L. Peiris tells parliament.
Police launch manhunt for suspected army deserters who stormed house in suburban Colombo and robbed 1.9 million rupees worth of cash and jewellery at gun point on Monday night.

Supreme Court rules Broadcasting Authority bill tabled in parliament by government inconsistent with constitution and to become law, has to be passed in parliament with a two-thirds majority and be approved at referendum.

Members of United National Party (UNP), which has 94 seats in Sri Lanka's 225-seat house and without whose support the bill cannot win a two-thirds majority, call for resignation of media minister after Supreme Court decision is announced in parliament.
The government will accept Supreme Court decision on proposed Broadcasting Authority bill and decide its next move accordingly, Industries Minister C.V. Gooneratne tells parliament.

Parliament will not sit on Wednesday as mark of respect for veteran pre and post-independence leader Wijayananda Dahanayake, whose funeral takes place today in southern Galle. Dahanayake, a former prime minister and parliamentarian for over 50 years, died last Sunday at 95.
Talks to end four-day strike by workers of Sri Lanka's monopoly gas distributor Shell Gas Lanka ends unsuccessfully on Tuesday. Talks will resume on Thursday, Labour Commissioner R. Wimalasena says.
UNP members, who opposed the government's Broadcasting Authority bill, burn copy of it after Court announced the bill as a whole was unconstitutional.
